lines.text: The Space Station flies only about 250 miles up, where gravity is still about 90 percent as strong as down here. So why doesn't it fall?
It does. It's falling all the time.
Throw a ball sideways and it curves to the ground. Throw it faster, and it lands farther away.
At about 17,500 miles per hour, the ground curves away as fast as the station falls, so it keeps missing Earth.
That's why astronauts float. They're not beyond gravity. They're falling right along with the station.
But a whisper of air up there slowly drags it down, so about once a month it fires thrusters to climb back up.
